act.name: Limitation Act, 1963
act.source_authority: Ministry of Law and Justice, Government of India
act.description: Central law governing time limits for suits, appeals and applications and exclusion or extension of time.

sections.title: Extension of prescribed period in certain cases.
sections.text: Section 5 permits delayed appeals or applications to be admitted on sufficient cause in the cases it covers.
sections.plain_language_summary: A court may excuse delay for certain appeals or applications if sufficient cause is shown.

sections.title: Exclusion of time of proceeding bona fide in court without jurisdiction.
sections.text: Section 14 provides for exclusion of qualifying time spent pursuing a matter in good faith before a court unable to entertain it.
sections.plain_language_summary: Time spent honestly pursuing the same matter in the wrong court may be excluded from limitation when conditions are met.

sections.title: Effect of fraud or mistake.
sections.text: Section 17 governs commencement of limitation where the claim involves fraud, concealment or mistake in covered circumstances.
sections.plain_language_summary: Limitation may begin later when fraud or mistake prevented discovery of the right or relevant facts.

sections.title: Effect of acknowledgment in writing.
sections.text: Section 18 governs a fresh limitation period following a qualifying written acknowledgment before expiry.
sections.plain_language_summary: A valid written acknowledgment made in time can start a fresh limitation period.

sections.title: Extinguishment of right to property.
sections.text: Section 27 provides for extinguishment of a property right when the limitation period for possession proceedings expires.
sections.plain_language_summary: Expiry of the prescribed period for a possession suit can extinguish the underlying property right.
